questions.q: What are Capacity Units (CUs), as introduced in Lesson 14?
options: A measure of storage only, unrelated to compute
A Power BI-specific billing unit with no connection to other Fabric items
A fixed monthly subscription fee unrelated to actual usage
The shared currency every Fabric operation spends — a KQL query, an Eventstream, a notebook run all draw from the same pool
questions.explain: Cost management is the practice of watching that consumption and understanding which parts of a pipeline draw the most.

questions.q: Why does a hopping window (Lesson 31) cost more in Capacity Units than a tumbling window covering the same data?
options: Hopping windows always use more storage, unrelated to compute
It recomputes overlapping aggregates continuously, touching each event several times, instead of once
Tumbling windows are actually more expensive in every case
There's no real cost difference between the two window types
questions.explain: Lesson 31 flagged this as an abstract tradeoff; this lesson turns it into a real, measurable dollar figure.

questions.q: What does a KQL Database retention policy do?
options: Prevents any new data from being ingested
Converts streaming ingestion into batch ingestion
Automatically ages out data past a defined point, rather than keeping every event forever by default
Increases the number of Capacity Units allocated to a workspace
questions.explain: The right retention period depends on how the data actually gets used — most queries only look at recent history.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does it actually mean to be "cost-aware" (one of Lesson 43's six production-readiness qualities)?
options: Cost-awareness only applies to Azure resources, never Fabric items
Knowing which specific choices — like a hopping window or long retention — drive cost, not just knowing the total bill amount
Minimizing cost at all costs, regardless of functional tradeoffs
Simply checking the monthly bill total once a month
questions.explain: Knowing the total bill tells you almost nothing on its own — the actionable version identifies specific cost drivers.

questions.q: What retention setting does the example .alter-merge policy in this lesson configure?
options: softdelete = 30d, aging out data older than 30 days
A retention period tied directly to Capacity Unit consumption
A setting that only applies to batch-ingested data
An unlimited retention period with no expiration
questions.explain: Thirty days might be generous for a dashboard only looking at the last hour, or necessary for a specific compliance requirement.
